public_rationale: The evidence shows that scaling can improve capabilities and that impressive reasoning results can remain limited in scope. Neither finding settles Marcus's necessity claim. Failure to demonstrate general intelligence so far does not establish that scaling can never deliver it; benchmark advances do not establish that it already has.
limitations: The capability target and paradigm boundary are not operationally defined.
The cited studies do not isolate every change made across successive AI systems.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: AI needs paradigm-shift innovation; simply scaling neural networks will not be enough.

statement.excerpt: The reality is that AI needs genuine, paradigm-shift level innovation. Simply building ever bigger neural networks won’t cut it.

from_speaker: AI needs genuine, paradigm-shift level innovation
Simply building ever bigger neural networks won’t cut it
our_interpretation: The surrounding discussion identifies the goal as general intelligence and robust common sense, including unfamiliar real-world situations.
The claim does not deny that larger networks can improve particular capabilities.
Scaling alone means increasing network size and associated training resources without introducing a fundamentally different method.
A paradigm shift must be identified independently of whether a system succeeds; success itself cannot be used to redefine its method as a new paradigm.
criteria.support_condition: Strong causal or theoretical evidence establishes that the relevant neural-network scaling approach cannot deliver the contextual goal and that a fundamentally different method is necessary.
criteria.contradiction_condition: An independently validated system achieves robust general intelligence and common sense through scaling the existing approach, with sufficient method disclosure to exclude an essential paradigm change.
